title: Tools That Reshape Their Users
sentences: We tend to describe a tool as something that extends an existing intention.
The account is flattering and only intermittently true.
A tool that is easy in one direction makes that direction feel obvious.
Over time, the obvious direction becomes the one we take without deciding.
Writing by hand and writing by keyboard produce recognisably different prose.
Neither is superior, but pretending they are equivalent is careless.
The interesting question is never whether a tool is good or bad.
It is which of our habits the tool quietly makes cheaper than the others.
Cheapness, repeated daily, does the work that argument cannot.
By the time we notice the change, we have usually stopped being able to compare.
